audit_findings.title: Unquantified performance guarantee may be a direct claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: At least $32m claimed, equal to $0.79/share and 1.27% of the $2,516m base equity value; ultimate exposure is uncapped and unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any payment is a claim against cash and common equity that is absent from owner earnings and the valuation bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: While it is reasonably possible that we will incur a loss from the claim under the performance guarantee, we are unable to estimate the range of loss on this claim.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantee and claim are demonstrated, but a loss is only reasonably possible and the company cannot estimate its range. The filed $32m claim alone would not materially alter the valuation conclusion, but the uncapped exposure prevents establishing that the maximum effect is immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current damages calculation, legal probability assessment, contractual defenses, insurance coverage and indemnity recoveries; probability-weight the net exposure and rerun the equity bridge.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter contradicts an announced multi-year business exit
audit_findings.magnitude: $250.2m of segment assets, equal to 9.9% of the $2,516m base equity value; $237.2m FY2026 sales and $0 FY2026 operating income
audit_findings.mechanism: The runoff changes future owner earnings, working capital, exit costs, asset-sale proceeds and the operating perimeter supporting terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate that the wind-down of this segment will take approximately three to four years as the Legacy Commercial Programs’ existing customer contracts are terminated and its rotable assets are sold.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the valuation compounds consolidated FY2026 owner earnings without separately modeling a filed three-to-four-year exit. Current segment operating income is zero, but the asset base is large enough that recovery proceeds, working-capital release, impairments and wind-down costs are reasonably capable of changing value. The net direction cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Build a separate Legacy Commercial Programs runoff schedule covering contract earnings, termination costs, taxes, inventory and rotable recoveries, working-capital release and disposal proceeds; value only the continuing operations in terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Joint-venture guarantees create an unrecognized contingent claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Guarantee exposure unquantified; filed joint-venture investments are $49.0m and FY2026 joint-venture earnings are $7.2m
audit_findings.mechanism: A guarantee payment would reduce cash or equity value, while joint-venture earnings currently contribute to operating owner earnings and stakes_net is zero.
audit_findings.evidence: We are unable to estimate our maximum exposure under these guarantees as they are largely dependent on the volume of inventory purchase orders outstanding.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees and absence of a recognized liability are demonstrated, but no guaranteed balance, maximum exposure or evidence of probable default is supplied. The record therefore cannot establish materiality, although recognizing venture earnings without testing the associated contingent claim may overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain outstanding guaranteed financing and inventory purchase orders, venture liquidity, counterparty recourse and default terms; stress or probability-weight the net exposure as a separate equity deduction.

audit_findings.title: The FY2026 anchor may retain a nonrecurring bargain-purchase gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.5m, equal to 17.0% of the $173.1m anchor; if fully retained, computed base value overstatement is approximately $10.24/share
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring acquisition gain would inflate anchor owner earnings and every forecast year and terminal value derived from that anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2026, we recognized a bargain purchase gain of $29.5 million related to our HAECO Americas acquisition as the preliminary fair value of the identifiable assets acquired exceeded the total purchase price.
audit_findings.explanation: The $29.5m gain is demonstrated, but its inclusion in owner earnings is unresolved because no anchor normalization bridge was supplied. If retained, its scale is clearly material. The cash-flow statement reverses the gain in reconciling operating cash flow, but that does not prove the separate owner-earnings calculation removed it.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $173.1m anchor line by line and confirm removal of the $29.5m bargain-purchase gain and $9.8m headquarters-sale gain with consistent tax treatment; rerun all scenarios if either remains.

audit_findings.title: Latest-year earnings contain partial acquisition periods against an ending claim base
audit_findings.magnitude: $270.1m aggregate purchase prices; acquired businesses represented 7.6% of FY2026 sales and 11.8% of year-end assets
audit_findings.mechanism: Partial-period acquisition earnings enter anchor owner earnings, while ending shares and financing represent the post-acquisition capital claims; pro forma earnings, interest, working capital and maintenance investment may move value in different directions.
audit_findings.evidence: On November 3, 2025, we acquired the outstanding shares of HAECO Americas, LLC and its subsidiary HAECO Airframe Services, LLC (together, “HAECO Americas”) from HAECO USA, Inc. for a purchase price of $ 78.0 million, which includes estimated post-closing adjustments for cash, working capital, and indebtedness.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated and large enough to affect the valuation. Full-year acquired operating earnings may raise the anchor, while normalized financing costs, recurring integration expense, working-capital requirements and maintenance investment may offset or reverse that effect. The supplied record cannot determine the net direction without a pro forma owner-earnings calculation.
audit_findings.action: Construct a full-year pro forma owner-earnings baseline for all four acquisitions, remove acquisition gains and transaction costs, retain recurring integration costs and financing expense, and include normalized working-capital and maintenance-capex requirements before rerunning the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Accrued acquisition consideration may require a separate cash-claim reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.1m recognized liability, equal to $0.20/share and 0.32% of the $2,516m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A settlement not already captured through owner earnings or working capital would require a one-time deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of May 31, 2026, we have a contingent consideration liability of $ 8.1 million, which was classified as Other accrued liabilities on our Consolidated Balance Sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is demonstrated, but even a full incremental $8.1m deduction is only 0.32% of base equity value and would not alter the valuation conclusion. The actual adjustment could be smaller or zero if the expense or future payment is already captured in owner earnings or working-capital treatment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the Trax liability and expected settlement through historical owner-earnings adjustments and working capital; deduct only the portion not otherwise captured and avoid double counting.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2020 residual $41.4m and FY2024 residual $33.9m; FY2026 residual unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to owner earnings, increasing the historical series or FY2026 anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $41.4m (94.7% of filed D&A); FY2024 $33.9m (82.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement is indicated because unidentified D&A remains an expense. The supplied residuals are substantial historically, but the valuation uses FY2026 latest actual rather than a historical trend, and no FY2026 residual or evidence of eligibility is provided. The record therefore cannot establish a current valuation effect or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2026 filed D&A by asset class and identify any eligible non-economic component; rerun the anchor and scenarios only for amounts supported by filed depreciation schedules or equivalent records.
